Set persistent table previews

Source: R/preview.R
preview.Rd

Keep a compact console display while retaining every row and column.

  • preview(): Store a head/tail or interval display preference.

  • preview_headtail(): Store a preference for the first and last rows.

  • preview_interval(): Store a preference for evenly spaced rows.

  • unpreview(): Remove preview preferences and restore ordinary printing.

Usage

preview(.data, style = c("headtail", "interval"), n = 10)

preview_headtail(.data, n = 10)

preview_interval(.data, n = 10)

unpreview(.data)

Arguments

.data

An in-memory data frame, data.table, ordinary/grouped/rowwise tibble, or sf data frame. Collect lazy tables and convert other subclasses explicitly first. Apply previews separately to lists of tables.

style

For preview(), either "headtail" (default) or "interval".

n

Total number of data rows to display, defaulting to 10. Supply a positive whole number or Inf for all rows; omission markers do not count.

Value

A data frame, tibble, data.table, or sf data frame with the same rows, columns, values, row names, and grouping as .data. The preview functions add a tidystata_preview class and print preferences; unpreview() removes them.

Details

Reading a preview

Head/tail previews divide n between the first and last rows, giving any extra row to the beginning. Dots mark an omitted middle. Interval previews show approximately evenly spaced rows without separators. Both styles show the first row when n = 1, avoid repeating rows in short tables, and report the number of omitted rows in a footer.

Row numbers refer to the current table after filtering or sorting. Grouped tables share one display budget. Use print(x, n = Inf, width = Inf) to show all rows and columns without changing preferences. Previews affect console printing, not HTML widgets or GUI viewers.

Omission dots align with numeric decimal points (or the last significand digit when no decimal is shown) and the last row-number digit. Other columns, including numeric columns without displayed numbers, use centered dots. Without Unicode output, the markers use periods.

Keeping or removing preferences

Settings follow supported base subsetting/replacement, dplyr row and column operations, grouping (including rowwise), summaries, reframing and tidyr pivots. Those operations determine the resulting container and groups. Joins use the left input's settings; bind_rows() uses the first input's. Arbitrary third-party transformations and direct vctrs::vec_rbind() calls are not covered.

tibble::as_tibble(), as.data.frame() and column extraction remove the preview. Wrapping or unwrapping a data.table creates an independent copy; subsequent native operations such as := keep ordinary reference semantics. Column classes and labels are preserved.

See also

print_headtail() for one-time printing.

Examples

tb <- tibble::tibble(id = 1:30, value = (1:30)^2)
tb
#> # A tibble: 30 × 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
#>  1     1     1
#>  2     2     4
#>  3     3     9
#>  4     4    16
#>  5     5    25
#>  6     6    36
#>  7     7    49
#>  8     8    64
#>  9     9    81
#> 10    10   100
#> # ℹ 20 more rows

ht <- preview_headtail(tb)
ht
#> # A tibble: 30 × 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
#>  1     1     1
#>  2     2     4
#>  3     3     9
#>  4     4    16
#>  5     5    25
#>  ⋮     ⋮     ⋮
#> 26    26   676
#> 27    27   729
#> 28    28   784
#> 29    29   841
#> 30    30   900
#> # ... 20 rows omitted in the middle; use print(x, n = Inf) to show all rows.

dplyr::filter(ht, id > 10)
#> # A tibble: 20 × 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
#>  1    11   121
#>  2    12   144
#>  3    13   169
#>  4    14   196
#>  5    15   225
#>  ⋮     ⋮     ⋮
#> 16    26   676
#> 17    27   729
#> 18    28   784
#> 19    29   841
#> 20    30   900
#> # ... 10 rows omitted in the middle; use print(x, n = Inf) to show all rows.

preview_interval(ht, n = 5)
#> # A tibble: 30 × 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
#>  1     1     1
#>  8     8    64
#> 16    16   256
#> 23    23   529
#> 30    30   900
#> # ... 25 rows omitted between displayed positions; use print(x, n = Inf) to
#> # show all rows.

unpreview(ht)
#> # A tibble: 30 × 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
#>  1     1     1
#>  2     2     4
#>  3     3     9
#>  4     4    16
#>  5     5    25
#>  6     6    36
#>  7     7    49
#>  8     8    64
#>  9     9    81
#> 10    10   100
#> # ℹ 20 more rows
